purpose: Guselkumab is used to treat adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis, a skin condition that causes red, scaly patches. It is also used to treat adults with active psoriatic arthritis, which causes joint pain and swelling related to psoriasis. This medication helps clear your skin and reduce joint symptoms.
how_it_works: Your immune system makes a protein called IL-23 that causes the inflammation responsible for psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis. Guselkumab works like a targeted shield — it finds and blocks that specific protein so it cannot trigger the harmful inflammation. By calming this overactive immune response, your skin can heal and your joints can feel better.
common_side_effects: Upper respiratory infections like the common cold, headache, injection site reactions such as redness or pain where you give the shot, joint pain, diarrhea, stomach flu, tinea infections (fungal skin infections), and herpes simplex (cold sores).
warnings: Because this medicine lowers part of your immune system, you have a higher risk of getting infections — tell your doctor right away if you develop signs of infection like fever, chills, or a cough. Your doctor will test you for tuberculosis (TB) before starting this medication. Do not use live vaccines while on this drug. Tell your doctor about all your other medications and any history of serious infections, cancer, or immune system problems.
typical_dosing: For plaque psoriasis, the usual dose is 100 mg injected under the skin (subcutaneous injection) at week 0, week 4, and then every 8 weeks after that. For psoriatic arthritis, it is typically 100 mg every 8 weeks after the first two starter doses. Your doctor or nurse will show you how to inject it at home using the prefilled syringe or autoinjector pen.
